Known vulnerability names (e.g., "Log4Shell", "Snake", "EternalBlue") or non-CVE descriptions are NOT to be tagged as Vulnerabilities, even if they refer to a known flaw. Only exact CVE-YYYY-NNNN substrings are allowed.
- Weakness: a specific CWE identifier (e.g., CWE-89) or fundamental flaw class.
- Configuration: a specific product, software, component, or device explicitly stated or clearly indicated as AFFECTED BY or IMPACTED BY a vulnerability or weakness (e.g., the vulnerable product in a CVE entry, or the product/component listed as affected). This MUST be an exact verbatim substring from the input text denoting the affected product/component itself. Do NOT extract:
  * Generic filenames, IP addresses, ports, or arbitrary strings not clearly identifiable as affected products/components (e.g., "comadmin.dat", "104.155.149[.]103", "443", "winds.exe" are excluded unless explicitly named as a product/component).
  * Software, tools, or utilities merely described as USED BY ATTACKERS or in actor tradecraft (e.g., "Impacket", "KerberCache", "PowerShell" when actor-used) unless the text explicitly states they are the affected/vulnerable component.
  * Phrases that only describe a vendor or generic suite when a more specific affected product substring exists; align the extracted span to the exact affected-product phrase as conventionally annotated (e.g., if gold uses "Internet Communication Manager (ICM)" do not truncate to "Internet Communication Manager"; if gold uses "FortiOS" do not extract "FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiSwitchManager" as a single config).
  * Spans with no canonical CPE and no clear affected-product status should be omitted; never emit a Configuration with null normalized_id unless the exact substring is unambiguously an affected product/component per above.
- AttackTechnique: a MITRE ATT&CK technique ID (e.g., T1190, T1090.002, T1078, TA0011) or explicitly named attack method. Each distinct ID occurrence must be its own entity with only the exact ID substring (e.g., from "Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859)" extract "T1078" and "T0859" separately, not the whole phrase). Both sub-technique IDs (e.g., T1090.002) and parent technique IDs (e.g., T1090) are valid when explicitly present. Only exact MITRE ATT&CK T-code or TA-code substrings qualify; do NOT tag software/tool IDs such as S0508, S1063, S1054 as AttackTechnique.

1. All entity text MUST be an exact verbatim substring from the input text.
2. Provide 0-based start and end character offsets based on the input text. end is exclusive, so text[start:end] equals the entity text exactly.
3. For normalized_id, provide the canonical identifier if available (e.g., standard CVE ID, CWE-xxx, canonical CPE 2.3 URI for products, or T-code for ATT&CK); otherwise null. For Configuration, only use a CPE 2.3 URI when the substring is a clearly affected product/component; if uncertain, omit the entity rather than emitting null normalized_id.
4. Do not output repeated duplicate entries for the identical mention span.
5. Extract only entities that meet the strict definitions. Skip any span that does not clearly fit one of the four types per the rules.
6. For AttackTechnique, capture solely the exact ID token (e.g., "T1090.002", "T1078") as entity text, never the surrounding descriptive words.
7. Never infer or insert entities not present as exact substrings in the input text. Do not hallucinate configurations, products, vulnerability names, or technique IDs that are not explicitly written in the provided text.
8. Output ONLY the specified JSON schema fields per entity: id, text, type, start, end, normalized_id. Do not add fields beyond the specified schema (e.g., no "evidence", "notes", or other extra keys).

Those keys are STRICTLY FOR HUMAN REFERENCE IN THE EXAMPLES and MUST NOT be copied or generated in your output. Your output must never contain "evidence" or "notes" or any field outside the schema in Rule 8.
10.
